findings.claim: D13 says the cocharacter mu_y 'can be chosen so that its filtration over W(k) lifts the Hodge filtration of G_0'. The paper puts the filtration on D tensor K for the finite extension K/breve-Q_p, and mu_y is in general defined only over K. A mu_y defined over W(k)[1/p] would make its conjugacy class defined over breve-Q_p, so the local reflex field E would be unramified over Q_p. Condition (A) allows ramified E, for example G=Res_{F/Q_p}GL_n with F/Q_p ramified and a cocharacter that is non-trivial at a single embedding. findings.claim: Missed source gap in the proof of Lemma 4.3.8(1), on which S31 rests. The proof asserts that 'X_*(G^ab)_I is an extension of Z by X_*(Z^c_G/Z_{G^der})_I' and deduces from Proposition 4.2.3(5) that X_*(Z^c_G/Z_{G^der})_I is torsion-free. Taking I-coinvariants is only right exact. The map X_*(Z^c_G/Z_{G^der})_I -> X_*(G^ab)_I can kill torsion, so torsion-freeness of X_*(G^ab)_I does not pass to the subgroup term. Counterexample to the asserted general step: G = GU(V) for K/Q imaginary quadratic ramified at an odd p, with dim_K V = n odd. Then G^ab = {(nu,d): d·d̄ = nu^n}, so X_*(G^ab) = {(a,b1,b2): b1+b2 = na} with inertia swapping b1 and b2, and X_*(G^ab)_I ≅ Z. Here Z^c_G = U(1) and Z^c_G/Z_{G^der} ≅ U(1), so X_*(Z^c_G/Z_{G^der}) ≅ Z with the sign action and its coinvariants are Z/2. An extension of Z by Z/2 is not Z. The paper gives no other reason why X_*(Z^c_G/Z_{G^der})_I is torsion-free for the auxiliary G. The lemma itself survives: G_3 -> G is surjective with kernel C_1 = Z^c_{G_2} (central; G_3^der ≅ G^der), so 1 -> Z^c_{G_2} -> G_3^ab -> G^ab -> 1. In the coinvariant sequence H_1(Gamma, X_*(G^ab)) -> X_*(Z^c_{G_2})_I -> X_*(G_3^ab)_I -> X_*(G^ab)_I -> 0, the H_1 term is torsion and X_*(Z^c_{G_2})_I is torsion-free because Z^c_{G_2} is induced, so the first map is zero. Hence X_*(G_3^ab)_I is an extension of torsion-free groups.

findings.claim: Unrecorded gap in the proof of Lemma 6.2.1. The proof fixes an ARBITRARY maximal Q_p-torus T containing g_s and then asserts that g_u lies in the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup containing T. This fails in general. In GL_2 take g=[[1,1],[0,1]] in GL_2(Z_p), so g_s=1, and T a nonsplit (unramified elliptic) torus. Over its splitting field the two Borel subgroups containing T are swapped by Galois, but the only Borel whose unipotent radical contains g is the Q_p-rational upper-triangular one. The lemma is still true: choose a Borel B with g in B(F') over a finite extension, then a maximal torus T in B containing g_s, so that g_u lies in R_u(B). findings.claim: The verdict on sourceIssue E11 is right but its reason misstates the obstruction. The review says Poonen's theorems are 'stated for a smooth quasi-projective subscheme of P^n' and that 'a smooth chart is not quasi-projective for free'. But any chart can be shrunk to an affine (hence quasi-projective) neighbourhood of y~, and Theorem 3.3 of Poonen does treat quasi-projective X. What fails is that the cited Corollary 3.4 assumes X smooth, PROJECTIVE and geometrically integral, which is what keeps the curve through the point geometrically integral and still meeting the dense open. A fixer following the review could 'repair' the gap by taking an affine chart, and that does not work.
